item.title: Coulomb collision operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.18988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Properties of the Coulomb collision operator that have been found useful in plasma kinetic theory and plasma transport theory are gathered and reviewed, with derivations. The use of velocity-space coordinates appropriate to a magnetized (drift-kinetic) plasma is emphasized. Little of the material is new, although the derivations may be more detailed than is customary.
item.dc:creator: R. D. Hazeltine

item.title: Magnetic Reconnection Governs the Entire Lifecycle of Solar Eruptive Magnetic Flux Rope
item.description: arXiv:2610.19348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While magnetic flux ropes (MFRs) are widely accepted to exist prior to many solar eruptions, the physical mechanism responsible for triggering and subsequently driving their eruptions remains debated. Classical models commonly attribute eruption onset to ideal magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, particularly the torus instability, while magnetic reconnection is often regarded as a secondary process. Using high-resolution three-dimensional MHD simulations, we investigate the eruption of an MFR that forms self-consistently through flux cancellation driven by converging motions and photospheric diffusion following an initial shearing phase. The pre-eruption MFR rises quasi-statically and reaches a height where the decay index exceeds the classical torus instability threshold, yet the system continues to evolve quasi-statically without eruption. Instead, eruption begins only when the current sheet beneath the MFR becomes sufficiently thin for magnetic reconnection to set in. Increasing numerical resolution systematically delays the eruption onset, whereas the decay index at eruption onset remains nearly unchanged, demonstrating that the onset is governed by reconnection rather than torus instability. During the eruption, magnetic reconnection continuously converts surrounding sheared arcades into newly reconnected twisted flux that merges with the pre-eruption MFR and continuously to build the erupting MFR. A component-resolved analysis of the Lorentz force work further shows that the newly reconnection flux contributes predominantly to the main acceleration phase. These results demonstrate that magnetic reconnection plays a central role throughout the entire lifecycle of the eruptive MFR: it builds the MFR, directly triggers its eruption, and provides the dominant driving of the eruption.
item.dc:creator: Xinkai Bian, Chaowei Jiang, Qingjun Liu, Xueshang Feng, Pingbing Zuo, Yi Wang

item.title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions Near an Isolated Three-Dimensional Magnetic Null
item.description: arXiv:2610.20015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic null points define the magnetic field topology in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres, and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary three-dimensional (3D) resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. The governing MHD equations are solved self-consistently using a first-order local expansion of the magnetic and velocity fields about the null. For any given magnetic-null configuration, the equations admit a two-parameter family of stationary solutions, comprising multiple solution branches with distinct velocity topologies. Along these families, the velocity-null polarity can change at bifurcation points where the flow becomes effectively 2.5D. A single magnetic null can therefore support positive-radial, negative-radial, and spiral stagnation flows, with qualitatively different inflow, outflow, and rotational properties. The associated pressure and resistivity distributions are likewise determined self-consistently and vary across the solution family, demonstrating that they are coupled to the flow topology rather than prescribed independently. The generic solutions do not require the velocity and magnetic separatrices to coincide, allowing plasma to cross the magnetic fan separatrix and providing a local reconnective flow. These results demonstrate that, in the presence of nonuniform resistivity, the magnetic topology alone does not uniquely determine the associated stationary flow, pressure, or resistivity structure around a 3D magnetic null, revealing the nonlinear feedback between all macroscopic variables and resistivity. The constant-resistivity field-aligned and spiral field-crossing solutions identified previously are recovered as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Kuljeet Singh Saddal, Dieter H. Nickeler, Rodrigo Meneses Pacheco, Michaela Kraus

item.title: Flares and flux ropes: an entangled story
item.description: arXiv:2610.20056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar flares serve as standard candles for all magnetic-reconnection-based energy releases, and their consequences into the heliosphere can be modeled from first principles. This review presents the latest developments in modeling solar flares and their associated flux rope expulsions with state-of-the-art multidimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) descriptions. Observationally established ingredients beyond a single-fluid, thermal plasma evolution have been incorporated to varying degrees, and we highlight self-consistent efforts realized in "standard flare" setups.
item.dc:creator: Rony Keppens, Yang Guo, Wenzhi Ruan

item.title: Augmented reality system for visualising magnetic field topology and charged-particle trajectories in magnetic fusion plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2604.25426v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A cost-effective augmented reality (AR) system is presented for visualising three-dimensional magnetic field structures and charged-particle trajectories in magnetically confined fusion plasmas. The system presented in this study integrates an orbit-following simulation code with a marker-based AR framework using a web camera and the OpenCV library. By synchronizing the time step of the simulation with the frame rate of the camera, the trajectories are continuously updated and superimposed in real time onto the camera image. Through the interactive operation of manipulating the web camera, users can observe three-dimensional structures, such as magnetic islands, from various positions and viewing angles. Such an AR environment supports an interactive means of exploring three-dimensional spatial structures that can be difficult to interpret from two-dimensional representations alone. It also provides a common visual representation that can be shared through a display by researchers and students with diverse backgrounds in physics, engineering, and related fields. The developed system has been used in practical exercises at the JT-60SA International Fusion School, with exploratory feedback from students.
item.dc:creator: Akinobu Matsuyama

item.title: A Magnetothermodynamic Theory of Energy Transport In Collisionless Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2609.01471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Presented here is an exploratory conceptual framework with the aim of describing electromagnetic and thermal energy transport and transfer in collisionless plasmas in a coherent way, starting from an arrow-of-time perspective. That is, arguments about the transport of energy are fundamentally based on the idea that systems tend to fill the phase space available to them. First, we describe electric fields, magnetic fields, and plasma particles as interacting subsystems that are thermodynamically linked in specific ways. Second, we discuss the importance of the stochastic electric field in the transport of plasma particles down energy density gradients until the energy flux contributions from so-called electrothermodynamic (ETD) interactions become sufficiently uniform. Third, the logic of ETD transport is extended to a magnetized system invoking 2 types of magnetothermodyamic (MTD) transport: 1) transport of electromagnetic energy through stochastic Poynting flux and 2) plasma energy transport through stochastic drift energy fluxes associated with local ExB drift motion. The magnitudes of the ETD and MTD mechanisms are tied to local characteristic scales of the electric field fluctuations and critical scales are derived beyond which ETD mechanisms dominate MTD mechanisms. Finally, we discuss the interplay between electrothermodynamic and magnetothermodynamic equilibria (ETE and MTE), dynamics in the small critical scale (MTD) limit, and the potential relevance of this type of description to the problem of reconnection onset and scale coupling.
item.dc:creator: Dominic Payne

item.title: Assessing the effect of error field penetration during plasma current ramp-up in the DIII-D tokamak
item.description: arXiv:2609.04546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work provides evidence that established error field penetration threshold scalings remain applicable during plasma current ramp-up. In dedicated DIII-D experiments with imposed $n=1$ perturbations during extended $I_p$ ramps, an apparent empirical threshold is found between $2$ and $3$~kA of applied 3D coil current, above which MHD modes are seeded. The imposed perturbation couples to the rational surfaces present during the ramp, seeding near the $q=4$ surface and penetrating as an $m/n=3/1$ mode by the end of the perturbation phase. To interpret these observations, multi-machine penetration threshold scalings are combined with equilibrium-based overlap metrics from the GPEC code, including the in-situ error fields of the device. This modeling reproduces the observed onset in the amplitude scan and classifies mode seeding across a database of 12 ramp-up discharges spanning a range of plasma currents and densities. Across this database, the seeding appears to be controlled primarily by the applied 3D coil current rather than by the plasma current or its ramp rate. Accounting for the in-situ error fields is found to be important for reliable prediction. These results are consistent with the robustness of scaling-based penetration metrics when coupled to detailed 3D field modeling under transient ramp-up conditions, and suggest the importance of accounting for in-situ error fields when assessing additional externally induced perturbations. This work is motivated by future tokamaks in which transient, non-axisymmetric error fields can arise during startup, for example from runaway electron mitigation coils.
item.dc:creator: C. F. B. Zimmermann, E. M. Bursch, C. Paz-Soldan, J. M. Hanson, N. Leuthold, N. C. Logan, A. O. Nelson

item.title: Static spin exchange-correlation kernel of the uniform electron gas at finite temperature
item.description: arXiv:2605.16888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the temperature and momentum dependence of the static spin exchange--correlation kernel of the unpolarized three-dimensional uniform electron gas using variational diagrammatic Monte Carlo. The calculations cover metallic densities with Wigner--Seitz radii $r_s=1\!-\!4$ and temperatures $T/T_F=1/16\!-\!8$, where $T_F$ is the Fermi temperature. At low temperature, the calculated kernel approaches established ground-state parametrizations. Heating suppresses its Fermi-scale minimum and reduces its magnitude, while the relative momentum dependence evolves nonmonotonically through the warm-dense crossover. At the two highest temperatures studied, the spin kernel is nearly constant over $q \leq 2k_F$, where $k_F$ is the Fermi wave number. The charge kernel at $r_s=1$ retains pronounced momentum dependence under the same conditions, making a local approximation to the XC kernel more accurate in the spin channel over this interval. The directly sampled uniform response determines the XC free-energy curvature with respect to spin polarization, independently of a fitted polarization dependence. This curvature sets the interaction contribution to the free-energy cost of weak polarization and differs by several percent from the Groth--Dornheim--Bonitz parametrization at elevated temperatures. These results provide momentum-resolved reference data for finite-temperature spin-response theories and direct constraints on the spin dependence of thermal free-energy functionals.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Hou, Zhiyi Li, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen
